findings.finding: The +33 is spread capture, not an inventory bet. The bot earned 4.45 bps per $ against the Binance-anchored fair and paid 1.24 bps in fees; inventory contributed between +0.03 $ (anchored fair) and -2.93 $ (Delta mark) while ADA fell 468 bps, because the time-weighted position was only -14 contracts and showed no directional information (corr with the next 5-min return +0.016). Net-of-fee markout PnL is positive on every day and the 300 s markout costs only 0.41 bps per $.

The tax reading is the largest single term in money. A market maker's realised ledger is thousands of small wins and losses: gross winning fills +77.85 against a net +46.05, so the 30% VDA no-set-off reading taxes 1.7x the net gain and leaves 9.93 of the 33.29; the slab-on-net reading leaves 23.30. This hits the MM harder than the trend book and is unresolved (resource/07 Gate 0).
findings.numbers: after tax: slab 30% on net +23.30; VDA 30% on net gains (no expense deduction) +19.47; VDA 30% on gross gains, no set-off +9.93 (tax 23.36)

findings.finding: Pick-off fills are the largest controllable leak. 29% of the $ traded came within 5 s of a >= 3 bps Binance move into our resting quote; those fills captured 2.61 bps instead of 5.08 and netted 1.83 bps at 60 s against 3.53 for fills with no pre-move; their toxicity ratio is 0.75. This is the latency finding of the 21 Oct memo (0.55 s mainnet writes, 400 ms timer loop); pulls on imbalance and leans were already tested and failed their pre-registered tests, so the remaining lever is reacting faster, not quoting differently.
findings.evidence: t2_by_premove5s.txt; cex-mm/artifacts/research/2026-10-21-live-stage1-2-tick-pickoff-latency.md findings 1 and 4; 2026-10-21-binance-imbalance-pull-replay.md (pull/away fail OOS); 2026-10-25-inventory-lean-replay.md (lean fails prereg)
findings.money_at_stake: 4.27 $ over the window (~0.68 $/day, 13% of PnL) if those fills earned what the calm fills earn

findings.finding: High-volatility minutes carry half the volume and earn the least. In the top tercile of Binance 1-min realised vol (> 10.7 bps/min) the bot traded 51% of its $ at capture 3.84 and net60 2.78 with toxicity 0.62, against capture 5.20, net60 3.89, toxicity 0.12 in the calm tercile; by the hour's ADA range the top tercile made 1.45 bps per $ (exact PnL incl. inventory) against 5.2 in the other two. The same pattern holds on trailing 5-min vol. Fast markets are where the 4.5 bps Binance tick runs over a 5 bps quote.
findings.money_at_stake: 4.89 $ at net60 (~0.78 $/day) if T3 fills earned T1's net60; up to ~16 $ on the exact (inventory-inclusive, noisy) numbers

findings.finding: Hour of day: the US morning (13-16Z = 18:30-21:30 IST) brings the most fills (2,000, 31% of $) at the lowest capture (3.26-4.35) and highest toxicity (0.54-0.78); 22-23Z and 1Z are the weakest hours (hour-23 net60 +0.24, hour-22 toxicity 1.54, hour-1 total -0.21 $). But the hourly exact PnL has sd 0.54 $, so a 6-sample hour-of-day mean has SE 0.22 $ and no hour is reliably negative; the daily shape (IST 0-5h thin and noisy, IST 19-22h busy) is not a scheduling edge yet.

findings.finding: Inventory is a risk, not a return, and it is within the design. The bot sat at the 600 cap 15.7% of the time (one side off), at >= half the cap 53%; mean |q| 315 contracts (~$65, 20% of equity); the worst equity drawdown was 2.88 $ (0.93%) and the longest under-water spell 10.3 h; the cap was overshot once to 754 on the 42b5eef run. Sells' 300 s markout (-1.61) vs buys' (+0.80) in a -560 bps window is a trend artefact. The lean replay found no PnL in leaning, so there is nothing to change at this size.

findings.finding: The 13 Oct 'whole-order fills are the informed ones' pattern is gone under the anchored fair: whole-quote fills (48% of $) have a +0.05 bps 60 s markout and net60 3.03, partial fills 3.40, completing fills 2.99; 200-contract fills net60 3.01. Fill size no longer predicts adverse selection.

By run and build nothing separates the builds; the one weak run is stage 1 (100 contracts, cap 300, 4.9 h: net60 1.00, toxicity 1.13, +0.34 $) which contained the 14-15Z rally of 20 Oct. The 60.9 h 42b5eef run made +12.43 $ (3.41 bps per $), e8256a7 +8.75 $ (3.08), the current 2711fca run +4.75 $ in 22.9 h (2.80 bps per $, net60 2.24 but net300 3.98).

findings.finding: Capacity, not edge, bounds the money. At 2.8% of ADAUSD's turnover and with fills coming from queue position at the touch (lean memo finding 3), a bigger quote competes with the same taker flow; the plan's stage 3 is a second market. The AVAX shadow is not there yet (138 fills, net60 1.43, -0.37 at 1000 ms latency), and the market scan's wide-spread candidates are low-turnover meme perps.

limits: Six days, one regime: ADA fell 468 bps with hourly ranges mostly 40-150 bps and no stress day; the gate asks for four weeks for a reason. The 7-day bootstrap CI on $/day covers sampling noise only, not offer revocation, venue risk, regime change or capacity.

26 Oct (1,123 fills, 18% of the volume) has no Binance 1 s dump yet and the Binance REST mirrors are blocked by the sandbox proxy, so its fills have capture (via Delta mark x 1.000147) but no markouts, vol or range regime; it is in the day/hour/run exact-PnL tables and in the ledger, not in the net60 statistics.

The split between spread and inventory depends on the fair: with the Binance-anchored fair (basis = rolling median of the bot's own side-adjusted fill prices, so capture is ~5 bps by construction) inventory is +0.03 $; with Delta's mark it is -2.93 $. net60 moves 0.34 bps between the two (3.09 vs 3.44) because the anchored fair sits 1.85 bps above mark on sells but 1.16 on buys. Totals are invariant.
Delta's spot index equals the Binance close (median 0.00 bps), so 'Binance-anchored' and 'venue index' are the same reference here; mark is index-plus-funding-basis and sits 7.2 bps below Binance.

Markouts use the 1 s kline close of the fill's second (up to 1 s after the fill) and Binance spot moves in 4.5 bps ticks; mo1/mo5 are coarse. Inventory PnL in the day/hour/run/regime tables is accrued by time (position x fair change in the group's window), not caused by the group's fills; the side/fill-kind/size tables therefore show spread - fee only.
Regime terciles use the contemporaneous minute's realised vol (not strictly causal); the trailing-5-min version gives the same ordering. Day-cluster CIs rest on 6 clusters.
The venue equity series starts 22 Oct 09:26Z; the drawdown before that comes from the fill-based MTM path, which agrees (2.90 vs 2.88 $) where both exist.

Reconciliation events are taken from the memos; no reconcile-log scan of the 24-26 Oct runs was done here [UNVERIFIED]. The fills export ends 17:29:21Z at +578 while the venue showed +496 at 17:31Z; an 82-contract sell after the cut-off is inferred, not seen [UNVERIFIED].

Tax figures are models of three readings (slab on net, VDA on net gains, VDA on gross gains with no set-off) applied to Delta's per-fill realised cashflow rows; which applies is the CA's question, not established here.
Annualised figures are x365 of 6.27 days and are not forecasts; the Scalper Offer (27% of PnL) has unknown terms; the bot already trades 2.8% of the venue's ADA turnover.

findings.finding: The ADA book is capacity-bound, not capital-bound or edge-bound. The edge per $ is real and stable (3.4-3.6 bps over 6,281 fills, positive every day) and the return on the $325 account is +11% in six days, but the dollars are capped by how much taker flow reaches one 200-contract quote at the touch: our fills barely grow when the venue gets busy (share 8.1% in quiet hours, 1.3% in the busiest; elasticity 0.41). Doubling the quote from 100 to 200 contracts raised the share in the same 11-16Z hours from 1.28% (20 Oct, one day) to 1.99% (pooled 21-26 Oct), about 1.55x for 2x size, and the whole-quote first-hit rate fell from 62% to 44.5%. Fills scale sub-linearly with size.

findings.finding: The whole-quote sweeps are where the size upside is, and they are not (yet) more toxic. 44.5% of first hits on a fresh 200-contract quote take all 200 and carry 80% of the dollars; the tape shows 12% of prints at >=1,000 contracts carrying 79% of notional, so a 400-1,000 quote would be filled by sweeps that today pass through to the 47k-100k-contract ladder one tick behind us. Within 200 contracts the markout does not degrade with hit size (net60 3.1-3.8 bps in every bucket; whole-200 hits 3.53), and the stage-1 tick pick-off bucket (Binance moved >=3 bps toward us in the 2 s before) is now profitable at +5.3 bps net60 after the concurrent-edit fix and the anchored fair. What the 1,000+ contract sweeps do to a bigger quote beyond 200 is unmeasured: that is the whole uncertainty of the 5x and 10x rows.

findings.finding: Tax decides whether scaling is worth anything. A market maker realises thousands of small gains and losses: gross gains were 2.3x the net. Under the VDA-per-realised-gain reading with no loss set-off the bot keeps 30% of its net ($10 of $33); under slab-on-net it keeps 70%. Every row of the ladder shrinks accordingly ($265/mo base at 5x becomes $80 or $186). The CA opinion gated in resource/07 is a harder gate for the MM than for the trend book because of this gross/net ratio.

findings.finding: What breaks first when scaling is the risk envelope, then the single VM, not the API. (a) Capital and the cap: cap notional at 5x is $621 = 1.9x the account; at 2x leverage that is $310 of margin plus a jump buffer (ADA daily range median 5.6%, max 8.3% in the window; 1-h range p95 2.2%, max 5.4%); the known gap 'no notional-vs-equity cap and no liquidation-distance stop' (skill) becomes binding. (b) The $15 daily stop trips on normal variance at 5x (daily SD scales to $4.6-9.3). (c) Inventory PnL at the cap scales linearly: one hour at a 6,000-contract cap against a 2.3% move is -$29 versus the current run's -$0.87 inventory term over 22.9 h. (d) The 0.6 s edit latency is unchanged; the pick-off bucket is profitable today but the exposure per stale quote grows with Q (a 2,000-contract quote hit after a 4.5 bps tick is $0.19 per event, ~150 events/day). (e) Rate limits: 2.4% of the 5-min weight budget per symbol, so ~20 symbols before the 70% rule; the 2 vCPU / 1.8 GB VM already cannot run the fill simulator beside the shadow and the shadow writes ~1.15 GB/day for 4 symbols (18 Oct memo), so disk and RAM bind at 4-6 symbols. (f) The 47k-100k-contract ladder maker one tick behind us absorbs everything beyond our quote today; at 5-10x we take its flow and it can tighten (the pessimistic scenario).

limits: The sweep tail beyond 200 contracts comes from 50 public prints (10 of them >= 200) over 31 minutes on 26 Oct plus the shadow tape's mean; the 5x and 10x fill multipliers (4.0 / 5.65 on whole hits) could be off by a factor of two either way. The 100 -> 200 matched-hours comparison rests on one stage-1 day (20 Oct, a rally day).

The marginal-edge decay (0.9 bps per doubling base, 1.5 pessimistic, 0 optimistic) is an assumption, not a measurement: within 200 contracts the markout showed no decay, and nothing in the data says what >= 1,000-contract sweeps do to a bigger resting quote. The model also ignores the ladder maker's response and queue position lost on edits.

The ledger window is 6.26 days (5 full days) in one regime: ADA fell 2.5% over the window with a median daily range of 5.6%; the daily PnL SD ($1.86) is from n=5. STRATEGY.md 11.3 asks for >= 4 weeks live before scaling; this run has 6 days.
26 Oct fills are not markout-scored (Binance publishes the 1 s dump the next day); the net60 split by size covers 5,010 of 6,068 hits (20-25 Oct).
Capture is measured against Delta's mark (buys 2.75 bps, sells 6.92 on whole-200 hits), which embeds the Delta-below-Binance basis; the sum is right, the per-side split is not a side asymmetry.

Delta's fee tier / VIP / maker-rebate schedule and the Scalper Offer terms are [UNVERIFIED]: www.delta.exchange, india.delta.exchange and docs.delta.exchange did not resolve from this sandbox; base rates (maker 0.0002, taker 0.0005) come from the API product record and the 18% GST / 10% referral from the repo skill.

Rate-limit figures (20,000 weight / 5 min, place/edit 5) and the ~0.6 s mainnet edit latency are taken from .claude/rules/cex-mm.md and the 21 Oct memos, not re-measured here. Whether the Tokyo VM can reach fstream.binance.com for a futures reference is [UNVERIFIED].

Tax readings are models from resource/07 and the 2026-10-22 memo (themselves marked [UNVERIFIED]); the per-fill split uses the ledger's cashflow rows as realised segments, which may not be the basis a tax authority applies.

Second-market scores use market_scan.txt medians (8 samples, 15 s gaps) where available and a single ticker snapshot otherwise; funding, listing age and token quality (DOOD funding -0.31%/8h) were not analysed. Binance volumes are from Saturday 25 Oct daily klines.
